title_en: Brij Khurana, Fixed Income Portfolio Manager, Wellington
title_zh: Brij Khurana（Wellington）：低利率留下了什么——货币政策、AI资本开支与全球债市再定价
subtitle_zh: Wellington固收基金经理Brij Khurana解析货币政策的金融化后遗症、财富效应驱动的通胀与通胀挂钩债等新机会。

turns.zh: 美联储真正依赖的那些传统新凯恩斯主义（neo-Keynesian）或一般均衡模型里，他们想用利率去调控的那些东西，其实和利率本身的相关性并不高。

turns.en: And the most common thing is investment. And when we think about investment, obviously there's housing investment, which is very correlated with interest rates, but you could argue that's almost an asset price rather than real form of investment.
turns.zh: 最典型的就是投资。说到投资，显然有住宅投资，它和利率高度相关；但你也可以说那更接近一种资产价格，而不是真正意义上的投资。

turns.en: And then what I'm really talking about is non-residential investment, which should be the thing that is very correlated with interest rates.
turns.zh: 我真正想说的是非住宅投资，它本应与利率高度相关。

turns.en: And probably historically it has, but in the last 25, 30 years or so, really since the internet bubble crashed in 2000 and 2001, investment has been its own cycle.
turns.zh: 历史上可能确实如此，但在过去25、30年里，实际上自2000、2001年互联网泡沫破裂之后，投资几乎自成一个周期。

turns.en: Hello, this is Dean Kernott and welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital in the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 你好，我是Dean Kernott，欢迎收听Alpha Exchange。在这个节目里，我们探讨金融市场的各种话题，涉及风险管理、收益创造，以及另类投资行业的资本配置。

turns.en: My guest today on the Alpha Exchange is Bridge Corana. He is a fixed income portfolio manager at Wellington Management. Bridge, it's a pleasure to welcome you to the podcast today.
turns.zh: 今天请到Alpha Exchange的嘉宾是Brij Khurana，他是Wellington Management的固定收益投资组合经理。Brij，非常高兴今天邀请到你。

turns.en: Thanks for having me, Dean. I saw your well-written piece in the FT about a month ago that was really linking monetary policy to the wealth effect.
turns.zh: 感谢邀请，Dean。大概一个月前我读了你在FT上写的那篇文章，写得很好，把货币政策和财富效应（wealth effect）联系了起来。

turns.en: I wanted to connect with you and solicit your insights and analysis at such an interesting time that we're having this conversation with a significant backup in bond yields, monetary policy, and flux, so tons to talk about.
turns.zh: 所以我想联系你，听听你的洞见和分析。我们这次对话确实赶上了很有意思的时点：债券收益率大幅上行，货币政策也充满变数，可聊的东西太多了。

turns.en: Give us a little bit of sense of your day-to-day at Wellington. You run an unconstrained go anywhere bond fund. Tell us a little bit more about that.
turns.zh: 先给我们讲讲你在Wellington的日常吧。你管理一只无约束、全球找机会（go anywhere）的债券基金，多介绍一下。

turns.en: It's an interesting time to be a bond portfolio manager for sure. As you mentioned, I run an unconstrained strategy, so it's really go anywhere.
turns.zh: 现在做债券组合经理确实很有意思。正如你所说，我管的是一个无约束策略，真的是哪儿有机会就去哪儿。

turns.en: We go where the opportunities are. It could be in rates. It could be in credit. It could be in currencies. Historically, 10 years ago when I first came to Wellington, a lot of my time was actually spent on the credit markets because that is where the opportunities are.
turns.zh: 机会在哪儿我们就去哪儿。可能是利率，可能是信用，也可能是汇率。十年前我刚来Wellington的时候，大部分时间其实花在信用市场上，因为那时机会在那里。

turns.en: Increasingly, my days are focused on G10 rates because that's been the asset that's been extraordinarily dislocated relative to the last few years and even obviously relative to history.
turns.zh: 现在我越来越多的精力放在G10利率上，因为相对于过去几年、当然也相对于历史，这个资产出现了极度错位（dislocation）。

turns.en: So I know that everyone thinks we're going to go back to the yield environment we were. At least we are back to the levels in the 1990s and early 2000s.
turns.zh: 我知道大家都觉得我们会回到过去的收益率环境。至少我们回到了1990年代和2000年代初的水平。

turns.en: From our standpoint, it has been a significant repricing. The drawdown in Fixed Income has been one of the worst in history. And so as I said, I'm spending a lot more time on rates markets now than credit.
turns.zh: 从我们的角度看，这是一次大幅的重新定价，固定收益的回撤堪称史上最差之列。所以就像我说的，我现在花在利率市场上的时间远多于信用。

turns.en: Well, I'm plenty older than you are, but my own start in the career was 1991. And I worked in Fixed Income Research at Nemora. And I got onto the desk and the tenure yielded eight and a quarter.
turns.zh: 我可比你的大多了，我入行是1991年，在Nomura做固定收益研究。我记得刚上交易台时，国债收益率是8.25%。

turns.en: Think inflation was 4%. So you had a giant term premium. So who knows? Maybe we just haven't seen the highs yet in yield. I was just pulling up the five-year real yield today.
turns.zh: 通胀我记得大概是4%，所以那时期限溢价巨大。谁知道呢，也许收益率的高点我们还没看到。我今天还专门把5年期实际收益率调出来看。

turns.en: And I was just trying to see what does the six months change? And it's been about 100 basis points of the last six months increase. Actually, I think it's 130, which is one of the highest increases of a six-month time horizon.
turns.zh: 我想看看过去六个月的变化，大概是上行了100个基点。实际上我想是130个基点，这是6个月时间跨度里最大的涨幅之一。

turns.en: But when I pulled the data back to 1995 or 1996, whenever the five-year tip was first issued, the real yield was 3.5%. So it was a good reminder.
turns.zh: 但我把数据拉回1995或1996年，也就是5年期TIP最早发行的时候，实际收益率是3.5%。所以这真是一个很好的提醒。

turns.en: As high as they look right now today, obviously back in the 90s, they were, as you said, 8% rates and 4% inflation. So real yields could also certainly be a lot higher.
turns.zh: 眼下的收益率看起来很高，但90年代就像你说的，利率8%、通胀4%，所以实际收益率当然也完全可能比现在高得多。

turns.en: Well, we're going to talk a lot about the here and now about the US rate environment, the global rate environment. This is not specific to the US.
turns.zh: 我们会花很多时间谈论当下：美国的利率环境、全球的利率环境。这不是美国独有的现象。

turns.en: What's happening here, it's a developed market sovereign phenomenon. And we'll bring in your FT piece. You wrote another piece, which I really wanted to start with, which was entitled, What Half Low Rates Wrought?
turns.zh: 正在发生的是发达市场主权债层面的现象。我们会谈到你在FT写的那篇文章。你还写过另一篇，我特别想从它聊起，题目是《What Have Low Rates Wrought?》。

turns.en: And it's an analysis of the reality that for the past 25 years, many of them have been spent with the policy rate stuck at zero with negative real yields.
turns.zh: 那篇文章分析了一个现实：过去25年里，政策利率在很长一段时间里卡在零，实际收益率是负的。

turns.en: You make this point, and it's certainly resonated a ton with me, which is monetary policy is supposed to be an economic instrument. It's supposed to get to the growth and inflation, but it really does have profound financial market impacts.
turns.zh: 你提出的这个观点真的让我特别有共鸣：货币政策本来应该是一个经济工具，本该作用于增长和通胀，但它确实对金融市场有着深远的影响。

turns.en: That's where I really wanted to start, which is when Warsh or Powell or Bernanke has a press conference, the man on the street isn't watching, but you are.
turns.zh: 我特别想从这里聊起：无论是Warsh、Powell还是Bernanke开记者会，普通人不会看，但你会看。

turns.en: I am as well. The markets care a ton, probably too much about what the Fed is doing. Walk us through your thought process and writing that piece and how you think about the interaction between monetary policy and markets.
turns.zh: 我也会看。市场非常在意美联储在做什么，可能在意得过了头。带我们走一遍你写那篇文章时的思路，你是怎么看待货币政策和市场之间的互动的？

turns.en: I think the impetus for that piece really came from just my experience trading markets for the last 25 years. And the conventional neo-Kansi in our general equilibrium models that the Fed really relies on, ultimately, I thought that the things that they were targeting with interest rates actually were not highly correlated with interest rates themselves.
turns.zh: 我想这篇文章的缘起，其实来自我过去25年交易市场的亲身经历。美联储真正依赖的那些传统新凯恩斯主义一般均衡模型——我后来认为，他们想用利率去调控的那些东西，其实和利率本身的相关性并不高。

turns.en: And the most common thing is investment. And when we think about investment, obviously, there's housing investment, which is very correlated with interest rates.
turns.zh: 最典型的就是投资。说到投资，显然有住宅投资，它和利率高度相关。

turns.en: But you could argue that's almost an asset price rather than real form of investment. And then what I'm really talking about is non-residential investment, which should be the thing that is very correlated with interest rates, and probably historically it has.
turns.zh: 但你也可以说那几乎是一种资产价格，而不是真正意义上的投资。我真正想说的是非住宅投资，它本该与利率高度相关，历史上可能也确实如此。

turns.en: But in the last 25, 30 years or so, really since the Internet bubble crashed in 2000 and 2001, investment has been just almost its own cycle.
turns.zh: 但在过去25、30年里，实际上自2000、2001年互联网泡沫破灭之后，投资几乎自成一个周期。

turns.en: So in the 2000s, there wasn't a lot of investment. People were still dealing with the implications of the Nasdaq crash where there was investment, was really abroad in China and other economies because of outsourcing, etc.
turns.zh: 2000年代投资并不多，大家还在消化纳斯达克（Nasdaq）崩盘的后果。有投资也主要发生在海外，在中国和其他经济体，因为外包转移等等。

turns.en: And then after the GFC similar, it didn't matter how low or negative real rates went. It wasn't stimulated to investment because there were so many losses on bank balance sheets that that wasn't the priority.
turns.zh: 金融危机（GFC）之后也类似——实际利率降到多低、甚至负值都没用。投资刺激不起来，因为银行资产负债表上亏损累累，那根本不是他们的优先事项。

turns.en: They were focused on securities purchases compared to actual lending. And I think even in our own time horizon, what's interesting is interest rates, in my mind, are really high.
turns.zh: 他们把重心放在买证券上，而不是真正的放贷。而且我觉得就我们眼前这段时间来看，有意思的是，在我看来利率其实已经很高了。

turns.en: And yet there is almost no correlation to the AI CapEx investment that we're seeing. And so the models are very much based on this idea that we lower interest rates, we get investment higher, even consumption through borrowing, etc.
turns.zh: 但我们看到的AI资本开支（capex）跟利率几乎没有任何相关性。而这些模型的核心逻辑恰恰是：降低利率，投资就会上去，消费也会通过借贷上去，等等。

turns.en: And growth picks up. And to me, those cycles are completely different. And then you have to start thinking about the secondary effects. Well, when you do create negative real rates, what that does is it encourages the financialization of the economy.
turns.zh: 增长随之回升。但在我看来，这些周期已经完全对不上了。接下来你不得不考虑二阶效应：当你制造出负实际利率时，它会助长经济的金融化（financialization）。

turns.en: It encourages, as you say us, people focused on what the Fed's next move is going to be. But certainly, I think also the amount of leverage in the system.
turns.zh: 正如你所说，它让大家只盯着美联储下一步会怎么走；而且我觉得它还助长了整个体系的杠杆水平。

turns.en: When we think after the 2000 recession, we saw a huge household re-leveraging boom because interest rates were very low in terms of the real cost of borrowing to buy houses at least in the early 2000s.
turns.zh: 回想2000年衰退之后，我们看到了家庭部门巨大的再加杠杆热潮，因为买房的实际借贷成本非常低，至少在2000年代初是这样。

turns.en: After the GFC, you didn't see a lot of borrowing in the economy, but you actually did see it from non-financial corporates who used it to buy back stock.
turns.zh: 金融危机之后，整个经济体的借贷并不多，但非金融企业确实在大举借钱，借来回购股票。

turns.en: You saw private equity certainly grow pretty dramatically and take advantage of a low rate environment to merge companies. And that has created, I would argue, less competition that has almost reduced the structural real rate for the economy.
turns.zh: 私募股权（private equity）显然大幅扩张，利用低利率环境去并购企业。而我认为这造成了更少的竞争，进而压低了经济的结构性实际利率。

turns.en: And then really after COVID, you went from the private sector borrowing, you went to the government borrowing because there wasn't a real cost to having massive fiscal stimulus that really just went to boost consumption rather than long-term real investment.
turns.zh: 到疫情之后，借贷主体又从私人部门转到了政府，因为大规模财政刺激好像没有真实成本，而这些钱主要用来提振消费，而不是长期的真实投资。

turns.en: And the very long-winded answer to your short question is that there's this lack of correlation between investment and interest rates has caused central bankers, when they missed their inflation target, to drop rates too low.
turns.zh: 对你那个简短的问题，我这个很长的回答是：投资和利率之间缺乏相关性，导致各国央行在通胀不达目标时，把利率降得过低。

turns.en: And then I would actually argue that the increase in financialization has decreased the potential growth rate of the economy. We have too much financialization, less focus on the real economy.
turns.zh: 我其实还想说，金融化的加深反而降低了经济的潜在增长率。金融化过度，对实体经济的关注就少了。

turns.en: And so they're just all wrapped up in a way that I think policymakers wouldn't necessarily assume. And if we go back to that period, that post-crisis, post-GFC period where forward guidance was well embedded in the structure of rates, non-emergency QE was done for years, post-GFC.
turns.zh: 所以这些因素纠缠在一起，其方式恐怕是政策制定者未必会假设的。如果我们回到危机后、后金融危机那段时期，前瞻性指引（forward guidance）已经深植于利率结构之中，非紧急状态的QE在金融危机后持续了好几年。

turns.en: At some point, there was a conversation among policymakers. I want to say the BIS had a lot of thought process on this, which is that low rates, when you get taken as low as we did, and of course, Europe took them negative for years, the deposit rate, that they can actually be in some ways deflationary, that you reduce the capacity to earn on savings.
turns.zh: 政策制定者之间后来有过一场讨论——我记得国际清算银行（BIS）在这方面想了很多——大意是：利率降到我们那么低的位置，欧洲更是把存款利率压成负值好几年，实际上在某些方面反而是通缩的，因为它削弱了储蓄赚取收益的能力。

turns.en: And so if you're trying to earn some income on your savings, well, you got to wait longer and longer when you get nothing. And I'm just curious if you have any thinking on that, as you kind of look at that period where investment was low, and it was a pushing on the string sort of episode in terms of keeping rates so low.
turns.zh: 如果你想靠储蓄挣点利息，在什么都挣不到的情况下，你就得越等越久。我很好奇你怎么看那段时期——投资低迷，利率压得那么低，却像是推绳子（pushing on a string）一样使不上劲。

turns.en: It's funny because it's a really long discussion in terms of why I think QE actually did create reflationary impulses in the US versus Europe.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，要讲清楚为什么量化宽松（QE）在美国确实制造了再通胀（reflation）的冲动、在欧洲却没有，得说很久。

turns.en: And I think it has something to do with the capital markets dominated economy we have in the US compared to Europe, which is bank led. And so I think that scenario really applies to Europe in particular in that in the US, because we're capital markets, if we ever went to negative real rates, which we did, but if we actually had policy rates that were actively negative, I think US companies would borrow a ton and buy back their stock, et cetera.
turns.zh: 我觉得这和美国以资本市场主导、欧洲以银行为主导的经济结构有关。所以那种情形尤其适用于欧洲。在美国，因为我们是资本市场主导，就算政策利率真正转负——我们确实到过负实际利率——我认为美国企业会大举借钱回购股票等等。

turns.en: Compared to in Europe, when you went to negative rates, it did because the economy was so bank centric when the banks were losing money, they stopped lending as much.
turns.zh: 而在欧洲，利率转负之后，因为经济太依赖银行，银行亏钱之后就减少了放贷。

turns.en: And so I think you do see this almost there was a different reaction there. The question also with all the QE we did, I have a relatively strange view probably on the balance sheet than I think a lot of people do in the sense that I think a lot of people view the QE that was done over the last many years as primarily working through the balance sheet of monetary policy, the balance sheet channel, which is basically where market participants,
turns.zh: 所以两边的反应确实不一样。另外关于我们做了这么多QE这个问题，我对央行资产负债表的看法可能和很多人不太一样，甚至有点奇怪。很多人认为过去多年的QE主要通过货币政策的资产负债表渠道（balance sheet channel）起作用——

turns.en: when someone buys a lot of something, the price goes off. And so the argument was is that as the Fed was doing so much QE, they were bringing down yields.
turns.zh: 大意是市场上有人大量买入某样东西，它的价格就会被推高。所以那种说法是，美联储大规模QE压低了收益率。

turns.en: It's almost the opposite has happened. Whatever they did, the excessive amount of QE yields would rise. And so the balance sheet channel does not explain what's happening to bond markets.
turns.zh: 但发生的几乎是反面：不管他们怎么做，QE规模过大，收益率反而上升。所以资产负债表渠道解释不了债市正在发生的事。

turns.en: And to me, what it is, is actually that when markets see a much larger balance sheet, they get very worried about the potential for debt monetization to take place at some point.
turns.zh: 在我看来，实际情况是，当市场看到央行资产负债表大幅膨胀，就会非常担心债务货币化（debt monetization）在某个时刻真的发生。

turns.en: It's a less responsible central bank than one with a smaller balance sheet. I think we would all agree that a Fed balance sheet at $6 trillion is more responsible than a $20 trillion balance sheet. And so investors want to buy reflationary hedges in an environment when there's a lot of QE and a lot of fiscal spending.
turns.zh: 资产负债表越大，央行就显得越不负责任。我想大家都会同意，6万亿美元的美联储资产负债表比20万亿美元的更负责任。所以在大规模QE和大规模财政支出的环境里，投资者想买再通胀对冲工具。

turns.en: And so ironically, QE in my mind causes bond yields to move higher because people sell bonds because they're not as excited because bonds offer a fixed income compared to stocks.
turns.zh: 所以讽刺的是，在我看来QE反而推高了债券收益率，因为人们会卖债券——相比股票，债券只是固定收益，他们没那么有热情。

turns.en: And so in the US, I think most people would say the reason stocks rose after QE is because bond yields went down, discount rates were lower, so asset prices need to go up.
turns.zh: 在美国，多数人会说QE之后股市上涨是因为债券收益率下降、贴现率更低，所以资产价格需要往上走。

turns.en: I actually think it's the opposite. Discount rates went up. They went up because people wanted to buy stocks, which is a reflationary asset compared to bonds.
turns.zh: 我其实觉得恰恰相反。贴现率是上升的，之所以上升，是因为人们想买股票——和债券相比，股票是再通胀资产。

turns.en: When you look back on the last 20 odd years and you have that period post the GFC, you have core PCE just one to one and a half percent and the central banking crew is worried it's too low and they're going to try to raise it by buying the country's bonds.
turns.zh: 回望过去20多年，金融危机后那段时间，核心PCE只有1%到1.5%，央行那帮人担心太低，还想通过购买本国国债把它拉上去。

turns.en: And now we've got something higher and it's not a supply chain thing anymore. You can't really point to the 2022 surge in inflation that was definitely linked to supply disruption. So it's here now, it's stickier. What have we learned about the inflation process from a learning standpoint? What can we conclude drives inflation? What are the driving forces that are pushing inflation to levels that are much higher than we saw, let's say a decade ago?
turns.zh: 现在通胀更高了，而且不再是供应链问题。你不能再把现在的通胀归因于2022年那波飙升——那确实和供应中断有关。眼下的通胀更黏。从学习的角度，我们对通胀过程明白了什么？能得出什么关于通胀驱动的结论？是什么样的力量把通胀推到了比十年前高得多的水平？

turns.en: I think the supply story, as you say, that's kind of in the rear view mirror. And I think from here it really is, and that was the purpose of the FT article, is that it is mainly wealth driven at this point, at least in the US. And the way I would say that is if you look at inflation, take out shelter, which once again, is more of an asset price than it is necessarily a reflection of core price pressures, it is close to about 2% over the last three years. So we had this big shock
turns.zh: 我觉得正如你所说，供给端的故事已经翻篇了。接下来——这也正是那篇FT文章的主旨——至少在当前，通胀在很大程度上是财富驱动的，至少在美国如此。我的说法是这样的：你看通胀，剔除住房（shelter），而住房同样更像是资产价格，未必反映核心价格压力——过去三年剔除住房的通胀差不多就是2%左右。所以经历了疫情那样的大冲击之后……

turns.en: for COVID core CPI X shelter has been around 2%. And where is that coming from? Like I should argue that the labor market is certainly the Fed can still credibly say that the labor market is not the source of inflation in the economy. We have a very low unemployment rate in the US, but that's only because labor supply is so weak at the same time labor demand is so weak.
turns.zh: 疫情以来，剔除住房的核心CPI一直在2%左右。那通胀是从哪儿来的？我认为，在就业市场方面，美联储现在仍然可以有底气地说，就业市场不是这个经济体通胀的来源。美国失业率很低，但那只是因为劳动力供给很弱的同时，劳动力需求也很弱。

turns.en: But when those both take place, that just means less nominal income coming into the economy. And so I would argue that if you look at the indeed wage tracker, there's all these other things that wages are not the source of inflation, which is really the demand side inflation that the Fed should be concerned with. And so where is the inflation? In my mind, it's the residual things from a lot of fiscal spending historically. So that's changed the relative prices of things
turns.zh: 当这两件事同时发生，意味着流入经济的名义收入更少。所以我认为，如果你去看Indeed的工资追踪数据，各种迹象都表明工资并不是通胀的来源——而工资通胀恰恰是美联储本该关心的需求侧通胀。

turns.en: like used cars versus new cars, certainly the wealth effect in things like shelter, in things like medical care and things like restaurants travel. That's where the inflation is this almost like sticky services inflation, which is much more tied to the wealth effect than it is to just demand side labor inflation, which to the Fed's credit, that was what we were seeing in 2022 and 23. They raised rates to five and a quarter or five and a half. I'm
turns.zh: 那通胀在哪儿？在我看来，它是历史上大量财政支出的遗留效应。它改变了相对价格，比如二手车对新车；也通过财富效应体现在住房、医疗、餐厅和旅行这些项目上。通胀就出在那里——一种黏性的服务业通胀，它和财富效应的关联远大于与需求侧劳动力通胀的关联。说句公道话，2022、2023年我们看到的就是那种劳动力通胀，美联储把利率加到了5.25%或5.5%——

turns.en: trying to remember five and three eighths. I think that's where we got to with the Fed. And that did a great job of bringing the labor market back into balance. And so the labor market, I do think, is in balance. And the inflation that we do see in the system has less to do with the policy rate, which is what the Fed feels like its primary tool is. And I would argue the other things that it does on the more financialization side of the economy, which has driven asset
turns.zh: 我想想，是5又3/8%，我记得美联储大概加到了那儿。那确实有效地把就业市场拉回了平衡。所以我确实认为就业市场现在是平衡的。而我们看到的通胀，与政策利率的关系不大——尽管政策利率是美联储自认为的主要工具。

turns.en: prices to levels which relative to GDP, so you could argue that relative to growth, asset price growth has well exceeded actual nominal growth or real growth. And so I think that's where some of the Fed's other tools can deal with that type of inflation, while they're still primarily concerned about the policy rate.
turns.zh: 我想说，美联储做的其他事情更多地推动了经济的金融化，把资产价格推到了很高的水平——相对于GDP、相对于增长而言，资产价格的涨幅大大超过了实际的名义增长或真实增长。所以我认为，应对这类通胀，美联储的其他一些工具反而更管用，哪怕他们目前主要还是盯着政策利率。

turns.en: So when you say wealth effect, do you mean that, and it's a good thing, I think, that there's more stock market wealth in the US than ever before? Is that a part of it that folks are just sitting there long-sum version of the S&P, which has delivered just absolutely remarkable returns, especially the last, let's say, three years post the 22 tightening cycle?
turns.zh: 你说的财富效应，是指——我觉得这是好事——美国股市创造的财富空前之高吗？是不是因为大家手里都长期拿着标普（S&P），而标普在过去三年、也就是2022年紧缩周期之后的回报实在太过亮眼？

turns.en: Absolutely. It's not only an income distribution story, it's a generational distribution story in the sense that the baby boom population controls goes to 50% to 60% of the wealth in the country. And it's really ironic because you would think that the older population, without being in retirement, should have this huge demand for fixed income.
turns.zh: 没错。这不仅是个收入分配问题，还是个代际分配问题——婴儿潮（baby boom）一代掌握着全国50%到60%的财富。特别讽刺的是，你会以为临近退休的年长人群应该对固定收益有巨大需求。

turns.en: And it's actually the opposite that if you look at the asset allocation for the baby boom generation, it's close to 70%, 75% stocks. I think at the country level, we have more wealth now in stocks compared to real estate for the first time historically. And so obviously, high wealth is a great thing, obviously. We want to be a very wealthy country, that's a good thing.
turns.zh: 但事实恰恰相反：你看婴儿潮一代的资产配置，股票接近70%、75%。我想在国家层面，股市财富超过房地产财富，这在历史上是第一次。当然，财富丰厚是好事，谁都愿意住在一个富裕的国家，这是好事。

turns.en: I would just argue that we are in this world where when you look at wages, wages of a percent of GDP have gone down over time. And so Secretary Besant talks a lot about real economy versus Wall Street. And I think it'd be helpful to grow into the level of wealth we have in the country in some ways, in that right now, this distribution that we're seeing is driving a lot of the inflation.
turns.zh: 我只是想说，在当今这个世界，你看工资占GDP的比重，长期在下降。Bessent财长经常谈实体经济对华尔街。我觉得，让增长去匹配这个国家现有的财富水平，从某些意义上反而是好事。因为眼下这种分配格局，正是通胀的重要推手。

turns.en: And it would be much better to see real wage growth increase at the current level of asset prices. I think that would be probably the most desirable policy outcome.
turns.zh: 在现有资产价格水平上，如果能看到实际工资增长提上来，那是好得多的局面。我想那大概才是最理想的政策结果。

turns.en: So from your perspective, where would you say we are with regard to the Fed cycle in terms of where it needs to go? I think last I checked, there's three-ish additional policy tightening priced into let's say twos, something like that, could even be four at this point.
turns.zh: 那在你看来，就美联储这轮周期还需要走到哪儿而言，我们现在处在什么位置？我记得前阵子看，比如2年期利率里已经定价了大约三次加息，现在甚至可能有四次。

turns.en: We're getting there. Yeah. Yeah. That's embedded. Do you think that that needs to be followed through on with respect to inflation? In other words, if monetary policy is a blunt tool, it's very indirect sometimes. It's, as you say, maybe more financial than economic, but it's what we have. And it's what Warsh's has to do, I think, is goals of using the balance sheet, unwinding the balance sheet.
turns.zh: 我们正在走到那个位置。对，这些已经内嵌在价格里了。你觉得从通胀角度看，这些加息需要兑现吗？换句话说，货币政策是个钝器，有时传导非常间接；正如你所说，它也许更多是金融层面的而非经济层面的，但这是我们仅有的工具。而我认为Warsh该做的事，是把使用、拆解资产负债表作为目标。

turns.en: That's going to run into Scott Besin a little bit at this point. How would you characterize Fed policy now in terms of restrictiveness and then where does it need to potentially get to?
turns.zh: 这在眼下会和Scott Bessent有点撞车。你怎么刻画现在美联储政策的限制性？它又可能需要走到什么程度？

turns.en: I have some thoughts on the idea of restrictiveness and how I think Warsh is changing that definition. I guess I would say just on the directly to your question, I do think that there's a lot priced in for the Fed. And historically, when I was learning macroeconomics, it was always the two main reasons you cause a recession are tight monetary policy and then commodity price shocks that temporary cause real wages to go down. And what's interesting to me is we're getting both of them.
turns.zh: 关于限制性这个概念，还有我认为Warsh正在改变它的定义，我有些想法。直接回应你的问题：我确实觉得市场对美联储已经定价了很多。我当年学宏观经济学时，教科书永远说引发衰退的两大主因是紧缩的货币政策和大宗商品价格冲击——后者会暂时压低实际工资。有意思的是，我们眼下两个都占了。

turns.en: We haven't yet got the hikes. We've only gotten one from the Fed right now, but the market is now pricing in, as you mentioned, at least before this hike, close to 100 basis points of hikes, getting closer to the 5% level for the policy rate. And that's not only in the US, that's also a global phenomenon as well. Europe is pricing in 80 or so. Australia and New Zealand, all these markets are pricing in a coordinated global tightening cycle. We've had very, very strong
turns.zh: 加息本身还没全来，美联储到目前为止只加了一次。但就像你提到的，市场现在至少已经定价了接近100个基点的加息，政策利率在逼近5%的水平。这不只是美国，也是全球现象。欧洲定价了80个基点左右，澳大利亚、新西兰，这些市场都在定价一场协同的全球紧缩周期。过去一年增长非常非常强……

turns.en: growth for the last year, but you could also argue that some part of that is because we had a global loosening cycle for the last year and a half. And now we're going the other way as well. And so, I do think that when you think about a policy rate where the market's pricing getting close to 5, not there yet, but getting close to 5, that's not that far from where we were in 22 and 23 when inflation was 8%. We had consumer balance sheets that were just much healthier because of the
turns.zh: ……但你也可以说，其中一部分是因为之前一年半经历了一轮全球宽松，而现在风向转了。所以我确实认为，想想政策利率被市场定价到接近5%——还没到，但在接近——这和2022、2023年通胀8%时的水平相差不远。那时候消费者资产负债表健康得多，因为……

turns.en: significant amount of stimulus you had after the pandemic. And so, consumer balance sheets do not look as good as they did back then. The oil price shock is now, I think, really eating into real wages. If you look at real wages, X transfers, they're growing at a negative level year over year, which is very rare outside of recession. So, point being that there's these two positive impacts to the growth outlook, lower policy rates for the last year and a half and relatively low
turns.zh: 疫情后有大规模刺激。所以现在消费者资产负债表的状况不如当时好看。而油价冲击现在我认为正在实实在在地侵蚀实际工资。你看剔除转移支付后的实际工资，同比已经是负增长——这在非衰退时期是非常少见的。所以重点是，过去一年半支撑增长前景的两大正面因素——较低的政策利率和相对较低的……

turns.en: commodity prices are both going the opposite way now. And so, I think people are very optimistic about nominal growth continuing. And I would say that maybe we saw the peak amount of nominal growth over the last year and even in the US, I think the other part of that story has been fiscal and fiscal spending has been so front-loaded because of the one big beautiful bill for the first half of this year. But if we do get divided government come November, that has historically
turns.zh: 大宗商品价格——如今都在朝反方向走。所以我觉得人们对名义增长的延续非常乐观。我想，也许名义增长的峰值我们已经看到了，就在过去一年。即便在美国，这个故事的另一半是财政——受One Big Beautiful Bill的影响，今年上半年的财政支出严重前置。但如果11月真的出现分裂政府，历史上那……

turns.en: been very important inflections for bond markets where the market's quick to price and less stimulus than we've had historically. So, November, whatever it is, could be an important catalyst for markets.
turns.zh: 一直是债市非常重要的拐点，市场会迅速定价比过去更少的刺激。所以11月，无论结果如何，都可能成为市场的重要催化剂。

turns.en: So, it is global and we'll definitely talk about that. There's this really good page on Bloomberg. It takes forever to load, but it's MIPR, Market Implied Policy Rate.
turns.zh: 所以这确实是全球性的，我们一定会谈到。彭博上有一个特别好的页面，加载巨慢，叫MIPR，即市场隐含政策利率（Market Implied Policy Rate）。

turns.en: You hit that up and it's got a little column where it shows every country's yield curve, a tiny little chart and all of them do this. They're all up and to the right. So, we'll circle back to the global part because you're looking for global opportunities in your unconstrained portfolio on the US yield curve. So, clearly, there's a lot of feedback from the words of the the body language of the Fed in terms of how let's say twos move. Fed funds to twos and this is the
turns.zh: 打开之后有一栏，把每个国家的收益率曲线都画成一张小图，全都是这样——一路向右上方。全球部分我们回头再聊，因为你在无约束组合里要在全球找机会。先说美国收益率曲线：显然，比如2年期对美联储的措辞和肢体语言反馈非常多，从联邦基金利率到2年期，这就引出了那个……

turns.en: hall of mirrors discussion. Our twos following Warsh is Warsh taking information from twos. We can talk about that all day long. Tens and thirties are different. That's a longer time frame.
turns.zh: 镜像迷宫（hall of mirrors）式的讨论：到底是2年期跟着Warsh走，还是Warsh从2年期取信息，我们可以聊一整天。10年期和30年期不一样，那是更长的时间维度。

turns.en: I'm curious if you can walk us through how you think about the ways in which those two prices are set. Let's just say twos and thirties. There are different spokes on those parts of the yield curve. That curve is not inverted at all. Some people say you don't really get to the end of a tightening cycle until you invert. So, we haven't done that yet. Walk us through how you think about how these prices or these yields clear at different points on the curve.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，你能不能带我们梳理一下这两种价格是怎么形成的。就说2年期和30年期，收益率曲线不同区段有不同的定价逻辑。现在曲线完全没有倒挂。有人说，曲线不倒挂，紧缩周期就不算真正走到头，而我们还没倒挂。讲讲你怎么看待这些价格、这些收益率在曲线不同位置是如何出清的。

turns.en: Certainly, the front end very much motivated by the Fed and decisions tied to the expectations for what the Fed is going to do. What is interesting is to your question about the yield curve, twos tens has not yet inverted. What's interesting is that in forward space, so if you look at a year from now, it actually has inverted. So, the market's whatever, two year one year versus the 10 year out. So, the market's effectively saying that in my view, if the Fed does go through with
turns.zh: 当然，前端很大程度上是被美联储驱动的，定价绑定在对美联储行动的预期上。有意思的是，回应你关于曲线的问题：2年期对10年期现在还没有倒挂。但有意思的是，在远期空间——如果你看一年以后的远期——它其实已经倒挂了。所以在我看来，市场实际上是在说，如果美联储真的把这套加息走完……

turns.en: this, then you do get an inverted yield curve, which may indicate that if they do do this, then policy will be tight. In terms of the relationship to the back, and I think that is another thing that has broken down historically. Historically, we used to say, and I actually do think the rise in yields recently has been a repricing of the Fed. It's not about treasury supply as much people want to think it is. It's not about inflation expectations. Those are very
turns.zh: 那么曲线就会倒挂，这可能意味着如果他们真这么做，政策就会是紧的。至于前端和后端的关系，我觉得这也是历史上已经失效的联动之一。我们过去常说——而我确实认为最近收益率的上行是对美联储的重新定价，并不是大家想象的国债供给问题，也不是通胀预期。通胀预期非常……

turns.en: low. They're kind of assuming Fed credibility, getting back to 2%. So, most of it has been a Fed repricing and real growth story emanating out of AI. When I started my career as well, I forget my boss at the time, but he was basically like the 10 year, 10 year rate.
turns.zh: 低。它们基本上假设美联储有公信力、能回到2%。所以大部分是美联储的重新定价，加上源自AI的实际增长故事。我入行的时候也是这样，我当时老板的名字我忘了，但他基本上就是把10年期对10年期利率（10y-10y）当作标尺。

turns.en: And the reason I'm talking forward term sometimes is because it adjusts for the shape of curve over time. But the 10 year, 10 year rate should look kind of like nominal growth.
turns.zh: 我之所以有时用远期利率来讲，是因为它剔除了曲线形状随时间变化带来的影响。但10y-10年期利率大致应该和名义增长相当。

turns.en: And that actually applied well in the 90s in the 2000s is that if you looked at the 10 year, 10 year rate, it was around nominal growth. Right now, I think it's close to around 6.2% or something like that if you look at the 10 year, 10 year rate in the US, which is really, really high. And when I think about forward estimates for nominal growth, that looks almost 100 basis points too high to me. I would say real population growth is
turns.zh: 这在90年代和2000年代确实成立：你看10y-10年期利率，它大致围绕名义增长。而现在，美国的10y-10年期利率我看接近6.2%左右，这真的非常高。对照我前瞻估计的名义增长，它看起来高了差不多100个基点。我想实际人口增长……

turns.en: probably like a half a percent from here. And then you think about maybe productivity is another 1% or so. So maybe you're talking about a long term growth rate in the US about 1.5%.
turns.zh: 从现在起大概是0.5%左右，再加上生产率大概1%上下，所以美国的长期真实增速大概1.5%。

turns.en: Even if you think inflation is 2.5% over the long term that gets you to 4%. And then you have to take into account that we have a lot more debt now than we did back in the 90s. And so maybe that's another 100 basis points of term premia. The point is, is that gets you to kind of that five-ish, five and a quarter percent 10 year, 10 year yield. And as I mentioned, we're almost 100 basis points higher than that, at least in forward space. So that's to me how I
turns.zh: 就算你认为长期通胀是2.5%，加总也就4%。然后你还得考虑，我们现在的债务比90年代多得多，所以也许再加100个基点的期限溢价。重点是，这样算出来10y-10年期收益率大概在5%、5.25%上下。而我刚才说了，现在比那个高了差不多100个基点，至少在远期空间是这样。这就是我……

turns.en: think about the two points on the curve, the 30s versus the 10s. In both ways, I think there's a lot priced into both of them right now. So you're essentially suggesting that back-end rates are following front-end rates. It's a sequence of forwards sort of thing.
turns.zh: 看待曲线上这两个点的方式，30年期对10年期。两边我都认为现在已经定价了很多东西。所以你实际上是在说，后端利率在跟随前端利率，是一串远期利率的叠加。

turns.en: Is there any signaling impact where if the Fed continues to tighten, the back-end doesn't follow suit? And you start to perhaps see the back-end rally as a function of, hey, this is going far along here. And you could see the growth in inflation on a forward-looking basis could be lower. Is that the signaling effect where what the Fed is trying to achieve is the market's telling it it's working? I think that's correct. I think there's
turns.zh: 会不会有信号效应：如果美联储继续紧缩，后端不跟涨，反而开始反弹，好像在说'这走得太远了'，市场前瞻看到的增長和通胀会更低？也就是说，美联储想实现的，恰恰是市场告诉它已经生效了？我想是的。我认为要出现那种情形……

turns.en: two things that you would need to see that happen, which is almost like back to a 2018 type experience where the market is telling the Fed that it's a mistake to hike. And we haven't seen that yet. And we certainly haven't seen it in the bond curve, although it has flattened a bit, but we definitely have not seen it in the stock market. And so I think that's a very different environment than in 2018. It gives me a lot of parallels, actually, because at that point,
turns.zh: 需要看到两件事，差不多是回到2018年那种情景：市场告诉美联储加息是个错误。我们还没看到这一幕。债券曲线上肯定还没看到——虽然已经平坦化了一些——但股市上我们绝对还没看到。所以我认为现在的环境和2018年很不一样。其实它让我想起很多相似之处，因为当时……

turns.en: the Fed had just raised rates throughout 2018. I think they hiked three times. And I remember December 15th or so, it was the Fed meeting. And Powell at the time came off extraordinarily hawkish, saying, we're not anywhere near restrictive. We're going to continue to hike rates, blah, blah, blah. I think he was also trying to assert Fed independence at the time.
turns.zh: 美联储在2018年全年一路加息，我想加了三次。我记得12月15号前后是议息会议，Powell当时讲话异常鹰派，说我们离限制性还差得远，我们还要继续加息，云云。我觉得他那时也是在力证美联储的独立性。

turns.en: We had that Christmas sell-off on the 26th or whatever it was. Yeah, the day after Christmas. Where the stock market was down, goes like 20 plus percent, and then they did a complete U-turn.
turns.zh: 然后是圣诞节后12月26号左右那次暴跌。对，就是节礼日，股市跌了差不多20%多，然后他们来了一次彻底掉头。

turns.en: And to me, that's when the bond market will give that signal. In order for that to happen, the stock market almost needs to tell the Fed that if they go along this course of policy rate hikes, it will cause growth to slow down. Obviously, that's not in the price right now. I do think we will start to think about that in a few months from now after the election. And because of the fact that if rates are raised, it will slow growth. But right now,
turns.zh: 在我看来，那才是债市发出那种信号的时刻。而要做到那一点，几乎需要股市先告诉美联储：沿着这条加息路径走下去，增长就会放缓。显然这不在现在的价格里。我的确认为，再过几个月、大选之后，人们会开始思考这个问题，因为继续加息终将拖累增长。但现在……

turns.en: the market's not telling it that. Part of your essay was around this idea that low rate regimes, sometimes extremely low rate regimes, have not really sponsored a big capex cycle.
turns.zh: 市场并没有这样告诉它。你文章里有一个观点：低利率体制，有时是极低利率体制，并没有真正催生大的资本开支周期。

turns.en: And now we have something where rates are reasonably high, certainly in the context of the last couple of decades. And we've got this capex boom. Does monetary policy need to slow that capex boom to slow demand? Is that part of it? That was where the FT piece comes in, is that I think that the AI capex spending, I think some of it is starting to look a little bit circular in my view. That I think is where there is this big debate because you have
turns.zh: 而现在利率相当高——放在过去二十年里尤其如此——却有一轮资本开支热潮。货币政策需要给这轮资本开支降温来抑制需求吗？这是其中的一部分吗？——这正是那篇FT文章的落点。我认为AI资本开支，在我看来，其中一部分已经开始显得有点循环（circular）了。我觉得这正是大辩论的所在，因为眼下……

turns.en: a lot of lending that's taking place. And obviously, it's lending coming from some of the best companies in the world with some of the best balance sheets and they're borrowing against plenty of assets, etc. Some of the chip financing deals look fairly circular, which reminds me of how things were almost pre-GFC. So I'm not even thinking about the late 90s, but just the pre-GFC experience where you had lending that just didn't look as bank driven as
turns.zh: 大量的借贷正在发生。当然，这些借贷来自世界上最好的公司之一，资产负债表极好，也有充足的资产作支撑。但一些芯片融资交易看起来相当循环，这让我想起金融危机前夕的情景。我甚至不说90年代末，就说金融危机前那种体验：那时的借贷看起来不像本该有的、由银行主导的……

turns.en: it should have been. And I think there's this big debate in the policy community. One view that I think the Fed holds is this is great. Let's have this lending take place outside the banking institutions. If there are losses there, it doesn't infect the banking system the way that subprime infected the banking system in the GFC. I have a somewhat different view that we have this huge growth in loans, not to the underlying... Everyone says the banking system's losing out
turns.zh: 那种形态。我觉得政策圈里有一场大辩论。我认为美联储持有的一个观点是：这很好，让信贷发生在银行机构之外，如果出现损失，不会像次贷在金融危机时那样传染银行体系。我的看法有些不同：我们看到贷款大幅增长，并不是流向实体……

turns.en: to private credit as being the marginal lender out there. But actually, if you look at loans to non-depository financial institutions, NDFIs, that is increased by close to a trillion dollars of new loans in the last six or seven years. And so banks are effectively lending to private credit who is then lending in a lot of innovative or more questionable ways. And so my view from a regulator standpoint is that the reason the banks are doing this is because they get very
turns.zh: 大家都说银行体系正在把边际贷款人的位置让给私募信贷（private credit）。但如果你看对非存款类金融机构（NDFI）的贷款，过去六七年这部分新增了接近1万亿美元。所以实际上是银行在借钱给私募信贷，私募信贷再用各种创新型或更可疑的方式放出去。从监管角度我的看法是，银行这么做的原因是资本待遇非常……

turns.en: favorable capital treatment compared to actual making corporate loans. But at the same time, as a regulator, banks are very well regulated. And so it makes sense for almost that to take place more in the banking system. And so I think that actually the Fed is probably going to go the opposite way. They're going to reduce the capital ratio on these loans because historically, they have had very low defaults and they also are very low LTV loans from the bank perspective.
turns.zh: 比直接发放企业贷款优惠得多。但另一方面，作为监管者来看，银行是被监管得很好的，所以让这些活动更多发生在银行体系内反而合理。我认为美联储实际上很可能反其道而行：他们会下调这类贷款的风险资本比率，因为历史上这些贷款违约率很低，从银行角度看贷款价值比（LTV）也非常低。

turns.en: But I also don't think that's just the only purpose of capital ratios is not only to accurately reflect the risk of a loan. It's also to affect the overall credit that we're providing to the economy. And it's probably still early, but at least some of the financing deals do look a bit more questionable than we've seen in the last few years. And so I do think that's a role where the Fed has regulatory capability to raise those capital ratios and bring in more
turns.zh: 但我也认为，风险资本比率的目的不只是准确反映贷款的风险，它还要影响我们向整个经济体提供的信贷总量。现在也许还早，但至少有一些融资交易确实比过去几年见到的更可疑。所以我认为这是美联储有监管能力发挥作用的地方：提高资本比率，把更多信贷拉回……

turns.en: in the banking system where you can at least have some amount of oversight over it. When we studied economics in college, we learned about the crowding out effect.
turns.zh: 银行体系，至少让人对其保持一定监督。——我们大学学经济学的时候，学过挤出效应（crowding out）。

turns.en: And this was really government's crowding out private businesses. And it seemed as if the opposite might be happening, at least to some extent. People have different takes on it. Michael Symbolus from JP Morgan Asset Management put out a chart that went viral, essentially showing just how much AI capex was relative to treasury borrowing. Some others have taken a different view on just the way in which that chart was calculated, suggesting that the crowding out was
turns.zh: 那讲的是政府挤出私人企业。而现在看起来，至少某种程度上，发生的可能正好相反。大家各有看法。JP Morgan Asset Management的Michael Cembalest发过一张广泛传播的图，展示了AI资本开支相对于国债借款的规模有多大。也有人对那张图里挤出效应的计算方式提出不同看法，认为挤出并没有……

turns.en: not that significant. What is your view? Maybe this is just back to the backup and long-end yields. So certainly some part of it's the backup and two-year yields and the body language of the Fed. But do you see the demand? Let's just use hyperscalers as our catch-all for it. Their demand for capital. Is that a part of the firmness of the back-end? How do you put them into the mix of explaining it? Absolutely. I think it is a big reason. And I'll give you two reasons for it.
turns.zh: 那么显著。你怎么看？也许这又回到了长端收益率的上冲。当然，其中一部分是2年期收益率的上冲和美联储的肢体语言。但你看到需求了吗？我们就用超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）来统称这一类。它们对资本的需求，是不是后端坚挺的一部分？你怎么把它们放进解释里？——完全正确，我认为这是很重要的一点。我给你两个理由。

turns.en: The hyperscalers who are borrowing in the corporate bond markets, and we're going to have record IG issuance this year. Every day it seems like you're having record days, record months.
turns.zh: 超大规模云厂商在公司债市场借钱，我们今年要有创纪录的投资级（IG）发行量。好像每天都有创纪录的发行日、创纪录的发行月。

turns.en: But their belief is that the return on investment on AI, they don't care if they're borrowing at 6%, 7%, 8%. That to them is not that big of a deal because their view is that their return on this investment is going to be 30%, 40%. And so whether or not it's 6% or 8%, it doesn't really matter.
turns.zh: 但它们的信念是AI的投资回报率——它们不在乎借钱成本是6%、7%还是8%，对它们来说那不算什么，因为它们认为这项投资的回报会有30%、40%。所以到底是6%还是8%，真的无所谓。

turns.en: Obviously as a bond holder, it really matters because 200 basis points on a 30-year instrument or 20-year duration, whatever it is, is a lot of losses. It is definitely putting pressure on borrowing for other corporate issuers. I have another view on it as well, which is that the reason we own bonds is because when growth slows, then you want an asset that tends to do well in that environment, this negative correlation between stocks and bonds. But what's happening with the
turns.zh: 对债券持有人来说当然大有关系——30年期或者20年久期的品种上，200个基点的差别意味着很大的亏损。这确实给其他企业发行人的融资造成了压力。我还有一个看法：我们持有债券的理由是，当增长放缓时，你希望持有一种在那个环境里表现好的资产，也就是股票和债券之间的负相关。但正在发生的……

turns.en: AI investment that we're seeing is that companies are borrowing so much that there's no way that you're going to see a nominal growth slowdown. So therefore bonds become even less attractive because they're not going to hedge a slower growth environment. That's another way that you're also seeing AI spending has caused this higher correlation between stocks and bonds, which means that one should have less demand for bonds causing yields to move higher. So I think there's two ways in
turns.zh: AI投资是这样的：企业借了这么多钱，名义增长就不可能放缓。因此债券的吸引力反而更低，因为它对冲不了增长放缓的环境。这也是AI支出造成股票和债券相关性升高的另一个途径，而相关性升高意味着对债券的需求应该更少，从而推高收益率。所以我认为有两个途径……

turns.en: which it's one directly crowding out, other companies investing. The other side of it is making bonds less attractive as a hedge to growth, which is also another form of crowding out.
turns.zh: ……一个是直接挤出其他公司的投资；另一方面是让债券作为增长对冲的吸引力下降，这本身就是另一种挤出。

turns.en: I just had Amanda Lynam. She's the chief credit strategist at Goldman Sachs on the podcast. Talking about a similar theme, which is the supply and demand dynamics for corporate credit, USIG corporate credit, and just the breathtaking amount of capital that needs to be raised, she's of the view that there's plenty of capital around to satisfy the demand at a price. But it's back to, I use Meta as an example, if we're thinking about the corporate bond from a Merton model standpoint,
turns.zh: 我前几天请到了Amanda Lynam，她是Goldman Sachs的首席信用策略师，在我们节目里聊了类似的主题：美国投资级公司债的供需动态，以及需要筹集的资金的惊人规模。她的看法是，只要有价格，市场上就有足够的资本来满足需求。但这又回到——我拿Meta举个例子——如果我们用Merton模型的观点来看待公司债……

turns.en: you buy a corporate bond, you're short the option, you get paid a little premium. So Meta's long the option. They're buying kind of vol, and it's probably way too cheap. So this financing, as you said, is probably too low in some ways for them. It's not going to stop them even if rates go up. What an interesting time. It's global. So this is where I wanted to dig in with you is you're looking around the world for opportunities. And these sovereigns, the corporates within
turns.zh: 你买公司债，就是做空一个期权，收一点权利金。所以Meta是做中期权，等于在买波动率，而且这个波动率很可能便宜得过分。所以就像你说的，从某种意义上讲，它们的融资成本还是太低了，即便利率上行也拦不住它们。真是有意思的时代。而且这是全球性的。这就是我想跟你深挖的地方：你在全球范围内寻找机会。这些主权国家，以及这些国家里的企业……

turns.en: those countries have got different growth profiles, different inflation profiles. Give us just maybe the big picture of what you see, where you see opportunity, whether it's sector-based or country based. And then we can drill down to some of the specifics. There's two areas that I would highlight.
turns.zh: 增长前景不同，通胀前景也不同。给我们讲讲你看到的大图景，机会在哪儿，是按板块还是按国家，然后我们再往下钻细节。——我认为有两个领域值得强调。

turns.en: There are a lot of countries where the markets are pricing in very substantial hiking cycles, and it's almost like a mistake if they do it. And it reminds me of back in 2008 when the ECB hiked. That was a quintessential central bank mistake. When should you not hike? And I think the economic data in countries like Australia and New Zealand is not good. And unemployment's rising. Inflation is temporarily sticky, but it's supply side driven like it is
turns.zh: 很多国家的市场正在定价非常大幅的加息周期，他们真要加，几乎就是犯错。这让我想起2008年欧洲央行（ECB）加息那次，那是最典型的央行失误——什么时候不该加息？我觉得澳大利亚、新西兰这些国家的经济数据并不好，失业率在上升；通胀暂时偏黏，但和各地一样是供给侧驱动的……

turns.en: everywhere in terms of oil prices. And so the market's also pricing in an 8500 basis point regime increase in rates. We have the luxury now of being able to look abroad, find countries which might have variable rate mortgage markets where the pass through to consumption is very, very quick compared to the US, where balance sheets on the federal level look a lot stronger than they do in the US. Steep yield curve. And so in some cases, even when you hedge it back to dollars, you get
turns.zh: 比如油价。所以市场还在定价85个基点左右的利率中枢抬升。我们眼下有一种奢侈：可以看向海外，寻找那些拥有浮动利率按揭市场的国家——利率对消费的传导比美国快得多，政府层面的资产负债表看起来比美国强健得多，收益率曲线也更陡。所以某些情况下，即使对冲回美元，你能拿到的……

turns.en: better yields than you can on treasuries or corporate bonds. And so having a more global footprint and having the remit to be able to access those markets, I think, is really helpful in generating returns from here. The other area where I think there's just a positive structural inflection is emerging market local bonds. And so these are bonds obviously issued by EM countries in their own currencies. And if you look at EM inflation, certainly it's higher, but it certainly
turns.zh: 收益率也比美国国债或公司债更好。因此，布局更全球化、有权限进入这些市场，我认为对从现在开始创造回报非常有帮助。另一个我认为是正向结构性拐点的领域，是新兴市场本币债券。这些显然是新兴国家以本国货币发行的债券。看EM通胀，固然更高，但它确实……

turns.en: is supply driven. And they never saw the same amount of fiscal spending we saw in the developed world. They are the high policy rates to the fact that real rates are back to the four to six to eight percent, depending on the country level, policy rate relative to inflation. The currency is still in a lot of cases look very cheap on a real exchange rate basis for quite some time. And so that's in the asset class that has done very well. Last year, EM local bonds were up almost 18%.
turns.zh: 是供给驱动的。他们没有经历过发达世界那样规模的财政支出。高政策利率的另一面是实际利率回到4%、6%甚至8%——取决于各国政策利率相对通胀的水平。货币在很多情形下按实际汇率看已经便宜了相当长时间。所以这个资产类别过去表现非常好：去年EM本币债券涨了将近18%。

turns.en: Even this year, in a world where fixed income returns are flat to negative, EM local bonds are actually still higher on the year. And there's a lot of very positive political stories. I mean, if you think about just positive political developments around the world, we've had Argentina, Colombia, Hungary, we'll see what happens in Brazil election. But Chile, there's a lot of countries which have moved into much more positive political market friendly, less
turns.zh: 即便是今年，在固定收益回报接近零甚至为负的世界里，EM本币债券年初至今仍然是上涨的。而且那里有很多非常正面的政治故事。想想全球各地的积极政治进展：阿根廷、哥伦比亚、匈牙利，巴西大选我们走着看。还有智利，很多国家转向了更积极、对市场更友好、财政支出更少的……

turns.en: fiscal spending direction. I think we're still early innings in the EM local bull market potentially, but investors are still not very heavily allocated to the space.
turns.zh: 方向。我觉得EM本币牛市可能还处于早期阶段，但投资者的配置还远没有重仓。

turns.en: Back to just Australia for a moment. So just wanted to go back to what you're saying around the pass through on costs to the mortgage side so that these are more variable floating rate mortgages.
turns.zh: 回到澳大利亚，就聊一会儿。我想回到你说的成本向按揭端的传导——也就是那些浮动利率按揭占比更高的情况。

turns.en: And so is the idea that you could hike policy enough such that you cause destruction of growth and that could cause a rally in the back end? Is that the idea?
turns.zh: 所以，这个想法是：政策利率加得足够高，足以摧毁增长，从而可能引发长端反弹？是这么回事吗？

turns.en: That's the idea. Yeah, they're more susceptible to rate rises versus the US. I mean, one of the biggest problems we have, well, it's not a problem. It's also a benefit to the economy is that consumption is not very correlated to interest rates because we have fixed rate mortgages and most people in 2021, 22, when rates got so low, they locked in very low rates. And so when the Fed was normalizing policy, it was one of the reasons that they had to raise rates so high
turns.zh: 就是这个意思。对，相比美国，它们对利率上升更敏感。我们这儿有个最大的特点——说问题也不太对，它其实也是经济的一个好处——就是消费和利率的相关性不高，因为我们是固定利率按揭，大多数人在2021、2022年利率特别低的时候锁定了很低的利率。所以当美联储做政策正常化时，它不得不把利率加到那么高，这也是原因之一……

turns.en: to have some economic impact. I do think about that going forward is the front end of the US curve going to be much more volatile compared to other markets because to have the same economic impact, you have to hike rates a lot and or drop them a lot to cause some changes because consumption, at least in the US, is a much larger part of the economy and is relatively interest rate insensitive.
turns.zh: ……才能对经济产生影响。我确实在想，往前看，美国曲线的前端会不会比其他市场波动大得多，因为要达到同样的经济效果，你得大幅加息或大幅降息才能带来改变，毕竟消费在美国经济中占比大得多，而且对利率相对不敏感。

turns.en: And what about China? So is that an area of focus for you? We definitely look at their bond market. I think yields there are very low. If you look at five year rates there at 1.5%, I think relative to even other safe markets, when I say safe markets, I mean markets where for some reason people go to in times of safety like Swiss bond markets, et cetera, rates are even low relative to those markets as well. There's not that much to do.
turns.zh: 那中国呢？那是你们关注的领域吗？——我们肯定看中国的债市。我觉得那里的收益率非常低。看5年期利率只有1.5%，我认为相对其他避险市场也一样——我说的避险市场，是指人们出于某种原因在避险时涌入的市场，比如瑞士债市等等——利率相对那些市场也偏低。可做的空间不大。

turns.en: I think in Chinese bond markets right now, I had been surprised why yields are so low when nominal growth is still quite healthy and they have this huge export led boom right now. At the same time, the way the bond markets acting reminds me very much of the US and Europe after the GFC, which is a country in the midst of a balance sheet recession. And because they have a closed financial system, we don't really see it. But given how much housing prices are lower and how
turns.zh: 我其实一直纳闷，中国债市收益率为什么这么低：名义增长依然挺健康，眼下还有一轮巨大的出口驱动繁荣。但同时，债市的表现又让我非常想起金融危机后的美国和欧洲——像一个正处于资产负债表衰退中的经济体。因为他们金融体系相对封闭，我们感受不那么直接。但考虑到房价已经跌了这么多，以及……

turns.en: much of that is embedded in their banking system, and it was certainly the largest asset for households, it does seem like they are having difficulty stimulating household consumption, which is one of the characteristics of the balance sheet recession. So that seems like what the bond market is pricing in, which even given all that, rates seem very low to me there. But that's at least what the market's telling you is that they're in the midst of some kind of longer term deleveraging
turns.zh: 那在很大程度上还嵌在他们的银行体系里，而房产又无疑是家庭最大的资产。看起来他们确实很难提振家庭消费，这正是资产负债表衰退的特征之一。所以债市定价的似乎就是这个；即便如此，我觉得那里的利率还是显得很低。但至少市场告诉你的信息是，他们正处于某种更长期的去杠杆过程中……

turns.en: that you typically see after a housing bust. I want to talk about the UK and Japan. Japan, to me, is fascinating insofar as Scott Besen seems super interested in it, calling upon that international repo facility, telling us he's got this asymmetric information.
turns.zh: ……通常是房产泡沫破裂后你会看到的。——我想聊聊英国和日本。日本在我看来特别有意思，因为Scott Bessent似乎对它极其关注，提到那个国际回购工具（international repo facility），说他们掌握某种不对称信息。

turns.en: If I go back to August of 2024, you may recall August 5th, there was this, I'll just call it a VIX event, but it really started overseas. And it was this really significant rally in the yen that just caught everybody offside. Everyone was leaning the other way. It just shows you how interwoven these markets are, because VIX futures went bananas overnight, it spilled over into the US morning, it was a Monday. There's a lot of connective tissue there. And I think that's what
turns.zh: 回到2024年8月，你可能记得8月5号那次——我姑且叫它'VIX事件'——但它其实起源于海外。日元大幅走强，把所有人都打在了错误的一边，大家都在押相反的方向。这说明这些市场多么盘根错节：VIX期货一夜之间疯狂波动，蔓延到美国早盘，那天是个周一。中间的关联非常多。我想那也正是……

turns.en: Scott Besen so focused on this idea that maybe capital comes home, treasuries are sold, he's clearly worried about it. What do you see when you look at Japan? How does that fit into your overall risk mosaic? I do think Japan is very important to the bond market, but I remember that event really clearly. To me, though, when you look at Japanese holdings, and I think this is a broader take, is that the carry trade, when we think about the yen carry trade, we historically
turns.zh: ……Scott Bessent如此关注的：资本会不会回流，美债会不会被抛售，他显然很担心。你看日本时看到了什么？这在你整体的风险版图上怎么安放？——我确实认为日本对债市非常重要，那次事件我记得非常清楚。不过在我看来，看看日本人的持仓，我的看法可能更宽一些：套息交易（carry trade），我们说日元套息交易，历史上指的是……

turns.en: meant people short yen and go buy high yielding emerging markets. That's just not the case anymore. Whether those assets have gone, and it's not even going buying US treasuries that much, they are a big buyer of US treasuries, but foreign holdings of US treasuries have fallen over the last decade, at least relative to the amount of debt that we have. Where it has gone is to US stocks.
turns.zh: ……人们做空日元去买高收益的新兴市场，现在已经不是这样了。那些钱流向了别处——甚至也不怎么买美国国债。日本确实是美债的大买家，但过去十年外国持有的美债一直在下降，至少相对于我们的债务规模而言。流向的是美国股票。

turns.en: And so I think the August event of two years ago, what was interesting to me is that EM did okay in that environment, but really the yen carry unwind was much more correlated to US stocks than anything else. And so I do think it matters for bond markets. I wouldn't say that it doesn't. At the same time, it matters, I think, more for stocks now than it does for bonds. And I think what Secretary Besan is trying to do, which makes sense to me, is that Japanese investors own US assets
turns.zh: 所以两年前8月那次事件，我觉得有意思的是，EM在那种环境下还好，但日元套息平仓和美国股票的相关性远高于其他任何东西。我确实认为它对债市重要，我不会说不重要。但同时，我觉得它对股市的重要性现在大于对债市。而我认为Bessent财长想做的事——我觉得讲得通——就是：日本投资者持有的美国资产……

turns.en: largely unhedged. And so as much as Fixed Income has gone down in the last few years, yen has depreciated more. And so on a real basis, they've actually been okay holding foreign assets.
turns.zh: ……基本上没做汇率对冲。所以尽管过去几年固定收益跌了很多，日元贬值得更多，换算成实际基础，他们持有海外资产其实还行。

turns.en: And especially if they own US equities, they've won in both ways. They've won with stocks going up, and they've won by the end depreciating. But at the same time, that has also created less demand for their domestic assets, less demand for their own currency, because US has been such a one way trade. And so I think what Secretary Besan is trying to do is to just make that not a one way trade. And if it's not a one way trade, the hedging cost to buy US bonds is very punitive
turns.zh: 如果持有的是美股，那更是两头都赢：股票涨赢一次，日元贬又赢一次。但与此同时，这也造成对他们国内资产、对本币的需求变少，因为买美国资产成了一边倒的交易。所以我认为Bessent想做的，就是让这不再是一边倒的交易。而如果不是一边倒，对冲后买入美债的成本对日本投资者来说就非常苛刻……

turns.en: if you buy it on a hedged basis as a Japanese investor. And I think that applies to US assets in general. And so if they can stabilize the yen, the argument is then they would actually repatriate capital to the Japanese bond market, which I think what the administration would argue is that's the reason yields are higher. Now, there is another side of that, which is if the Japanese are buying less US bonds, someone else has to buy those bonds. There is a little bit
turns.zh: ——我是说，日本投资者如果做对冲买入，成本惩罚很重，我想这对美国资产整体都适用。所以如果他们能稳住日元，逻辑上资本就会回流日本债市——我想政府会说，这正是收益率更高的原因。但这件事还有另一面：如果日本人不怎么买美债，就得有别人来买。这里面有点……

turns.en: of cognitive dissonance there. But I think the bet they're trying to make is that this is less of a flow debate in who's the next marginal buyer, more about just stabilizing yields at already high levels. So I think that's the argument and that's why they're acting the way they are.
turns.zh: ……认知失调的味道。不过我认为他们想押的逻辑是，这与其说是谁当下一个边际买家的流量问题，不如说索性是把收益率稳定在已经很高的水平。我想这就是他们的逻辑，也是他们这么做的原因。

turns.en: And then just on the UK, and maybe we'll throw France in there as well, that certainly gets a fair amount of press these days, the spread of French bonds, the German bonds is blown out to 2012 before droggies, whatever it takes, speech. So that's not a good sign.
turns.zh: 再说英国，顺便把法国也带进来。法国最近确实占了不少新闻版面，法国国债对德国国债的利差已经拉大到2012年、Draghi那句whatever it takes讲话之前的水平。这不是好兆头。

turns.en: What do you make of, let's focus on the UK for a moment. They had that unwind in September 2022. I mean, the fiscal situation just seems very challenging.
turns.zh: 你怎么看？先聚焦英国吧。他们2022年9月经历过那次平仓。我的意思是，财政状况看起来非常棘手。

turns.en: They don't have the luxury of the depth of the US reserve currency and so forth. When you look at the UK from a bond market standpoint, what do you see?
turns.zh: 他们没有美元储备货币那种市场深度和条件。从债市角度看英国，你看到了什么？

turns.en: I think it is interesting to compare now versus the trust episode a few years ago, and that was certainly caused by the pension unwinds that took place at the time. And positioning is a lot cleaner in the UK bond market than it was back then. And in some ways, what they've done with their bond market is almost six to 12 months ahead of the US in terms of they've cut long issuance substantially, trying to bring in the way I'm pretty dramatically.
turns.zh: 我觉得把现在和几年前的Truss事件做个对比很有意思，那次无疑是由养老金平仓引发的。而现在英国债市的持仓干净得多。某些方面，他们在债券市场上的操作几乎比美国提前了6到12个月：大幅削减长期限发行，压降的方式相当激进。

turns.en: Japan did the same thing, by the way. The difference I think between the UK and other countries though, which makes us a little bit more excited about the back end of the curve there, is that they had a QT program going on, which was one of the few countries that did not just allow runoff, how we do in the US, but actually was selling bonds. And that's no longer going to be taking place to the same degree. I think there are more positives. And I think also,
turns.zh: 顺便说，日本也做了同样的事。不过我认为英国和其他国家的区别——也是让我们对英国曲线后端更兴奋一点的原因——是他们一直在做量化紧缩（QT），它是少数几个不像美国那样只让资产自然到期、而是真正在卖债券的国家之一。而这种情况接下来不会再以同样的强度进行了。我觉得正面因素更多了。而且我认为……

turns.en: in the US at least, we don't worry about 6% deficits. We don't worry about $2 trillion deficits. At least in the UK now, even left-leaning administrations are very focused in terms of making sure that they're receptive to the bond market. In some ways, that's a positive. I know the fiscal situation isn't great there, but at least they're taking heed of what we're saying in the bond market compared to the US, where we continue to spend money regardless of the
turns.zh: 至少在美国，我们已经不对6%的赤字率感到紧张了，也不担心2万亿美元的赤字。而在英国，哪怕是左翼政府，现在也非常在意要对债市保持敏感。某种程度上这是好事。我知道那里的财政状况不算好，但至少他们听得到债市在说什么。相比之下，美国不管……

turns.en: level of yields. And so I think there's more optimism one could have on the UK bond market than we've had in the last few years. And I think there's also now a lot priced into the front end of the curve there, where the BOE is expected to release, and bond market pricing is up about 85 to 100 basis points as well. So there's a lot priced into there. I think when it comes to France, it's a little bit interesting. Obviously, you have a lot of political risk there
turns.zh: ……收益率水平高低，照样花钱。所以我觉得，对英国债市可以抱比去年几年更多的乐观。而且英国曲线前端我认为也已经定价了很多——市场预期英国央行（BOE）会宽松，债市定价也上行了大约85到100个基点。所以那里已经定价了很多东西。至于法国，我觉得有点意思。显然未来几年政治风险很多……

turns.en: over the next few years. That spread to Germany is the highest level. But I think that it is also at a higher level than it was in 2011, because at the time, France had much better debt metrics than they do currently. They were also seen as the safe haven compared to the Italy and the Greece's of the world. And I think what's interesting is that in the last 10 or 15 years, other economies in Europe have actually deleveraged. Greece has obviously delevered,
turns.zh: 法国对德国的利差处于最高水平。但我认为，这个利差比2011年更高也是合理的：当时法国的债务指标远好于现在，而且相比意大利、希腊这些国家，法国还被看作避险地。有意思的是，过去10到15年，欧洲其他经济体其实是在去杠杆的。希腊显然去杠杆了……

turns.en: Italy has delevered as well, really punitive deflation in their own economies to get debt levels under control. And France has actually gone through a bit of a credit boom over the last 15 years. Bank lending has been robust there. Government borrowing has been quite dramatic.
turns.zh: 意大利也去杠杆了，靠的是国内相当痛苦的通缩才把债务水平压下来。而法国过去15年其实经历了一轮信贷繁荣，银行放贷一直很强劲，政府借款也相当大胆。

turns.en: And so it's not surprising to me, I guess, to say that the spread is much higher than it was in 2011. That makes sense to me. Now, I think with questions of where that spread could go, and some people are saying, well, why shouldn't it trade it where Italy was back in 2011?
turns.zh: 所以利差比2011年高得多，我并不意外，这说得通。至于这个利差可能走到哪儿，有人说：为什么不跌到2011年意大利的水平？

turns.en: I think that's also not a reasonable comparison, because at that time, we were talking about and really considering whether or not Italy would be leaving the eurozone. And I don't think that's possible for France. There are a lot more mechanisms in place for the ECB to buy French debt.
turns.zh: 我觉得这个类比也不合理。那时候我们真的在讨论、在掂量意大利会不会退出欧元区。我不认为法国存在这种可能。欧洲央行购买法国国债的机制比当年多得多。

turns.en: Some part of this is also just a higher rate story in Europe as well with more beta associated with France and other countries. So that spread makes sense that it is wider than we saw back then.
turns.zh: 其中一部分也是欧洲整体利率更高的故事：法国和其他国家的贝塔（beta）更大。所以利差比当年更宽，是合理的。

turns.en: But also, when we think about ranges, we shouldn't also price in some of the terrorist scenarios that I think people are discussing right now.
turns.zh: 但同时也想说，我们考虑利差区间时，不该把眼下人们在讨论的一些Truss式风险情景也计入定价。

turns.en: So bring it all together for us. So as a fixed income investor, you can only get your money back. So you want to be confident that that's the case. And so high growth is what helps the borrower get you paid back. But that often usually comes with higher inflation. So you get paid back, but perhaps not with the same strength of the currency that you hoped for. What's the big picture for you when you look at the global opportunity
turns.zh: 帮我们收个尾吧。作为固定收益投资者，你图的就是把钱收回来，所以你要确信这一点。高增长能帮助借款人把钱还上，但高增长往往伴随更高的通胀，于是你收回了钱，但币值的强度可能不是你希望的那样。当你审视全球机会……

turns.en: set versus, let's say a decade ago when you had, again, both growth and inflation so much lower. So maybe more risk on the growth side, but less risk on the inflation side. Bring it all together for us. I think that's why inflation link bonds are some of the most attractive assets in fixed income right now because it'd be silly not to say that we have much more inflation risk now than we've had over the last few decades. And yet, if you look at what the inflation link bond markets
turns.zh: ……和十年前相比，那时增长和通胀都低得多，也许增长端风险更大，通胀端风险更小。给我们讲讲全貌吧。——我认为这正是为什么通胀挂钩债券（inflation-linked bonds）是眼下固收里最有吸引力的资产之一，因为很明显，我们现在的通胀风险比过去几十年大得多。可你要是看通胀挂钩债市……

turns.en: are pricing in, break evens are pricing in, a return to break evens are basically at 2.3% throughout the whole curve. And so there isn't a lot of inflation risk premia in inflation link bonds. And you're at real rate levels that are basically the highest level except for when the asset class was first created in the 90s and you demanded this huge liquidity premia because people didn't know how to invest in them. So when I think about assets that if you have a longer term
turns.zh: 市场定价的盈亏平衡通胀率（break-even），全条曲线基本都在2.3%。所以通胀挂钩债里并没有多少通胀风险溢价。而实际利率水平基本上处于历史最高区间——除了90年代这个资产类别刚诞生时，那时大家要求巨大的流动性溢价，因为不知道怎么投它。所以在我看来，如果你的期限更长……

turns.en: time horizon and can protect capital, I think inflation link bonds would be close to the top of the list. If we do go through a gross slowdown, you're going to have wanted to own nominal bonds instead of inflation link bonds. But I think given just the current situation and the level of real yields, it's a little bit safer to play in inflation link bonds than other things. And so when I think about three areas of excitement in bond portfolios, that certainly is one
turns.zh: ……而且要考虑保护资本，我认为通胀挂钩债会是最优先的选项之一。如果我们真的经历严重增长放缓，你会希望自己持有的是名义债券而非通胀挂钩债。但就眼下的局面和实际收益率水平而言，投通胀挂钩债比其他品种更安全一些。所以要我讲债券组合里三个令人兴奋的方向，这肯定是其中之一。

turns.en: error we think is pretty exciting. I would say as we talked about already, global bonds focus in countries with really strong fiscal balance sheets that also might have a higher pass through of rates to the domestic economy to slow it down and keep rates stable. I think that's focusing globally. And then the third area, as I said, this longer term structural trend towards emerging market local bonds, I think those are the three areas that are the most exciting
turns.zh: 我们认为这一点就很令人兴奋。第二，就像我们已经聊过的，是全球债券——聚焦那些财政资产负债表非常强健、同时利率对国内经济传导更高、能把经济压下来并保持利率稳定的国家。全球层面就是这样的布局。第三个领域，就像我说的，是新兴市场本币债券这个更长期的结构性趋势。我认为这就是眼下最令人兴奋的……

turns.en: right now. Last question, I can't help but ask you. So that 2.3%, that break-even that's embedded in the pricing structure of TIPS. If you told me that was 3.3%, I probably wouldn't blink an eye, just given inflation credibility, I think is down a little bit. Concurrent inflation is 4%. Why do you think it is so low? Why is the market clearing at 2.3?
turns.zh: ……三个方向。——最后一个问题，我实在忍不住要问：这个2.3%、嵌在TIPS定价结构里的盈亏平衡通胀率，你要是告诉我它是3.3%，我大概都不会眨眼，就凭我认为略有下降的通胀公信力，而且当前通胀是4%。你觉得为什么它这么低？为什么市场出清在2.3%？

turns.en: It's the question we all ask ourselves in inflation link bond markets. It's partly because one TIPS trade like another inflation link bonds, they trade like a risk asset. When you don't want them to behave like a risk asset, they are more illiquid than treasury. So I think that is one part of the discount. I also think that they disappointed a lot of investors in 2022. So you had this year when inflation spiked dramatically and they very much outperformed
turns.zh: 这是通胀挂钩债市场里每个人都会问自己的问题。部分原因是，TIPS和其他通胀挂钩债一样，交易起来像风险资产。当你不希望它表现出风险资产属性的时候，它又比国债更不流动。所以我认为这是折价的一部分原因。我还觉得，2022年它们让很多投资者失望了。那一年通胀飙升，它们确实大幅跑赢了……

turns.en: nominal treasuries. At the same time, they still delivered negative total returns. And so you're also seeing, I think, just a move away from the asset class over time. So it's an under owned asset, I would argue, given valuations given the level of real yields. It trades like credit when you don't want it to trade like credit is probably the best answer to that enigma that's existed for quite some time. And that's where it helps to have a longer term time horizon,
turns.zh: 名义国债，但总回报仍然是负的。所以我觉得，随着时间推移，资金一直在远离这个资产类别。所以从估值、从实际收益率水平看，我认为它是一个被低配的资产。你不希望它像信用品那样交易，可它偏偏像信用品一样交易——这大概能回答那个存在已久的谜题。而这正是需要更长持有期限的地方……

turns.en: understanding that if growth slows, break evens will fall even more, but you're getting compensated at a level of real yield. And if you like the carry of the asset class, if we keep realizing these levels of inflation, given what's priced in, it's a much more attractive, caring asset class than I would argue credit with better liquidity. So that's kind of why we like them here. Bridget, it was a pleasure to host this conversation, taking us around the world
turns.zh: ……要明白如果增长放缓，盈亏平衡会跌得更多，但你获得的实际收益率补偿摆在那里。如果你喜欢这个资产类别的票息收益，而且通胀继续像现在这样兑现，那么相对其定价，我认为它是比信用品更有吸引力、流动性还更好的利差资产。这就是我们在这儿看好它的缘由。——Brij，很高兴这趟带你环游全球的对话……

turns.en: in global bond market valuations and dynamics. So thanks for being a guest today. Thanks for having me, Dee. You've been listening to the Alpha Exchange. If you've enjoyed the show, please do tell a friend. And before we leave, I wanted to invite you to drop us some feedback.
turns.zh: ……探讨全球债市的估值和动态。谢谢你今天做客。谢谢你的邀请，Dean。你刚才收听的是Alpha Exchange。如果你喜欢这个节目，请告诉一位朋友。在结束之前，我想邀请你给我们留点反馈。

turns.zh: 我们希望能借助这些对话，帮助投资社群加深对风险的理解，所以你的意见很宝贵，也为我们该聚焦哪里提供方向。
